title: Lexicographically Smallest Permutation Greater Than Target
summary: Given strings s and target of equal length n, find the smallest permutation of s that is lexicographically greater than target.
statement: Given strings s and target of equal length n, find the smallest permutation of s that is lexicographically greater than target. If no such permutation exists, return an empty string. A string a is lexicographically greater than string b if the first differing character in a comes after the corresponding character in b alphabetically.
constraints: s and target contain the same one to 300 lowercase-letter positions.
The answer must use exactly the multiset of characters in s.
Return the lexicographically smallest permutation strictly greater than target, or the empty string.
hints: The answer should match target as long as possible, then exceed it by the smallest available character.
Greedily consume an equal prefix, then backtrack from its end until some position can be raised.
At the chosen position take the smallest available larger letter and append all remaining letters in sorted order.
Trying positions from latest to earliest maximizes the equal prefix, and the sorted suffix is minimal once the first greater position is fixed.
editorial: Trying positions from latest to earliest maximizes the equal prefix, and the sorted suffix is minimal once the first greater position is fixed.

tests.explanation: Matching b then increasing the second position to c yields the smallest answer bca.
bbaa is the greatest permutation, so no strictly greater answer exists.
